hypothesis: Same build as base, timed WITHOUT profilers. In base, perf stat's inherited counters (sched-in hook on every context switch) cut light eth_call from 183k req/s (bare warmup) to ~49k req/s, so the bare run is the honest champion metric. Profiles come from base-symbols instead.
llm_commentary: Bare (profiling-off) hardware race of the unmodified release build: c8a 5.36s [5.37/5.35/5.35] beats c8i 7.17s (+34%) and c8g 8.90s (+66%), with ≤2% run-to-run spread on every box, so the ranking is solid. The workload is latency-bound on a few hot cores — MDBX B-tree seeks, keccak, per-SLOAD cursor churn and futex wakeups between tokio and the blocking pool — which favours the EPYC 9R45's higher clocks and larger L2 over Granite Rapids and Graviton4 at equal vCPU. Note the engine builds c8a with -C target-cpu=znver4 although the 9R45 is Zen 5, so znver5 is a free compiler-phase check. Next: exp-storage-cursor (reuse one storage dup cursor per provider) on all three families, then maxperf/PGO.
